system_description.narrative_title: A Tectonic, Interlinked Crisis: Markets, AI, Energy and Regional Wars
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where accelerating AI-driven economic concentration and a volatile bond market intersect with acute energy and maritime-security shocks and resurgent regional wars. Financial market flows, corporate strategies and national policy reactions feed back into each other — amplifying risks (soaring yields, market concentration, supply-chain stress) while political instability (elections, protests, hybrid attacks) reshapes alliance choices and military postures. The system is in flux: small shocks in shipping, oil logistics, or a high-profile cyber/terror incident cascade into market repricing and rapid diplomatic/military responses.
system_description.scope: Sovereign states and alliances, regional conflict zones and non-state armed actors, global energy and shipping networks, international financial markets and central banks, major technology firms and AI ecosystems, corporate supply chains, public opinion and domestic politics
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic-security order (interconnected international system of states, markets, corporations and transnational networks)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime logistics (oil, diesel, tankers, Strait of Hormuz/Horn of Africa routes)
International financial markets and macro-policy (sovereign bond markets, central banks, yields and investor flows)
Technology and AI industrial base (chip supply chains, AI models, corporate concentration and regulation)
Regional conflict complexes and alliance management (Middle East/Houthi-Iran axis, Russia–Ukraine and European security)

variables.name: Middle East regional war and maritime attacks
variables.description: Iran-backed proxies, Yemeni Houthi forces and Gulf partners (notably Saudi Arabia and allied states) are escalating cross-border strikes and attacks on aviation and shipping, shifting the regional security balance and disrupting energy and trade flows.

variables.name: Russia's war against Ukraine and European security pressure
variables.description: Russia’s renewed large-scale strikes and hybrid operations against Ukraine are intensifying military and political friction with Kyiv and neighbouring NATO states, reshaping European deterrence, defence posture and security cooperation.

variables.name: U.S.-China strategic competition in AI and semiconductors
variables.description: The United States and China are locked in a technology and supply‑chain contest—centred on advanced AI, chips and data governance—that is redirecting investment, export controls and industrial policy worldwide.

variables.name: Global bond-market stress and sovereign financing squeeze
variables.description: A synchronized rise in long-term yields and a sharp repricing of sovereign and corporate debt is putting pressure on governments and central banks, altering fiscal options and amplifying political and market volatility across advanced economies.

variables.name: Populist electoral realignments and political volatility
variables.description: Resurgent populist and right‑wing movements—exemplified by dramatic electoral swings and high‑stakes national contests such as in Brazil—are reshaping domestic politics, coalition dynamics and policy trajectories in multiple democracies.
